settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: The method is documented/used as a multi-line comment validator; in JS and CSS the only standard block-comment terminator is "*/" (and "-->"), so rejecting "*/" covers the conventional case.
No caller in this repository passes attacker data to this method; the API is consumed by external bundles not present here.
candidates.description: XSSAPIImpl.getValidMultiLineComment returns the caller-supplied comment verbatim whenever it does not contain the literal sequence "*/", and otherwise returns defaultComment. The method performs no other character filtering or encoding. If a consumer uses this value inside a JavaScript or CSS multi-line comment, an attacker controlling the input could inject a comment terminator with an alternative form or otherwise influence the surrounding code without using the exact token "*/". The check is purely substring-based and relies entirely on the caller placing the value in a comment context.
missing_evidence: No usage of getValidMultiLineComment within this repository; consumer code that determined the output context is absent.
No test or documentation of the expected output context (JS comment, CSS comment, etc.).
preconditions: A caller passes untrusted input to getValidMultiLineComment and embeds the returned value inside a JS/CSS block comment.
Attack input avoids the exact substring "*/" while still achieving breakout (e.g. via alternative terminators/encodings) or the consumer uses the raw returned text in a non-comment context.
candidates.title: getValidMultiLineComment only blocks '*/' (JS/CSS comment context breakout possible)

counter_evidence: The STRING alternative explicitly uses a negative lookahead against 'javascript\s?:', showing intent to block javascript: schemes in string-style URLs.
CSS token validation is documented per http://www.w3.org/TR/css3-syntax/ and returns defaultValue on non-match.
Modern browsers generally block javascript: in CSS url() contexts, and the AntiSamy policy is the primary filter for HTML content.
candidates.description: getValidStyleToken returns the input unchanged if it matches the composite CSS_TOKEN regex. That regex (lines 284-312) explicitly includes URL (url(...)), FUNCTION (identifier(...)), STRING, and dimension tokens. As a result tokens such as url(...) and calc(...) are considered 'valid' and returned as-is. The STRING alternative excludes the substring 'javascript:' via a negative lookahead, but unquoted url(unquoted) and functional tokens are not restricted to safe schemes inside the regex itself. If a consumer writes the returned token into a style/attribute context, scheme-based payloads (e.g. url(javascript:...)) rely on the negative lookahead only for the quoted-string branch.
missing_evidence: No caller in this repository uses getValidStyleToken; the actual output context is unknown.
No test cases exercise scheme-bearing url()/function tokens.
preconditions: A caller uses getValidStyleToken output inside a CSS value/attribute context.
Attacker input forms a token matching the URL/FUNCTION branch (e.g. url(...)) that carries a dangerous scheme not excluded by the regex.
candidates.title: getValidStyleToken accepts unquoted URL and function tokens by design

counter_evidence: Comments document deliberate exclusion of critical characters (x, u, semicolon) to avoid expression()/url()/statement breakout.
Only characters needed for hex and functional color notation are allowed; returns defaultColor otherwise.
No caller within this repository uses this method, so no reachable injection point is shown.
candidates.description: getValidCSSColor trims the input and returns it if it matches the regex (?i)[#a-fghlrs(+0-9-.%,) \t\n\x0B\f\r]+ (or the named-color regex [a-zA-Z ...]+). The comment states the design goal is to exclude 'x' (expression), 'u' (url) and semicolon. The first regex permits parentheses, commas, percent, +, -, ., #, and a subset of letters including h,l,r,s,f,g. This permissive set is relied upon to prevent CSS injection; correctness depends on the character-class choices rather than structural parsing.
missing_evidence: No demonstration that the allowed character set can form a dangerous CSS construct without x, u, or semicolon.
No consumer context in the repository.
preconditions: A caller uses the returned value in a CSS context where the allowed characters could be combined into a meaningful directive despite excluding x/u/;.
candidates.title: getValidCSSColor uses an intentionally permissive character class

counter_evidence: Recursion depth is bounded: the recursive call passes "" as the default, so at most one extra level occurs.
Exceptions from parsing are caught and only logged at debug level.
candidates.description: Both getValidJSON and getValidXML, on null or invalid input, call themselves again passing defaultJson/defaultXml as the new source and "" as the default. This recursion terminates only when the (possibly attacker-influenced or caller-supplied) default value is null/empty or itself valid. If a caller passes a default that is also invalid and non-empty, the methods recurse one extra level and then return ""; termination is guaranteed only because the second call uses default "" — but the design lets an invalid non-empty default be re-parsed. This is a robustness/DoS-adjacent concern rather than a clear injection.
missing_evidence: No caller in this repository passes attacker-controlled defaults.
preconditions: A caller supplies a non-empty, invalid defaultJson/defaultXml value.
candidates.title: getValidJSON/getValidXML recursive re-validation with default may loop/recurse on cyclic defaults

counter_evidence: isValidHref (XSSFilterImpl lines 127-155) also re-decodes/re-unescapes and runs the same AntiSamy containsAllowedValue/matchesAllowedExpression checks used by MagicSAXFilter.
Tests in XSSFilterImplTest assert javascript: and entity-encoded javascript: are rejected.
DEFAULT_HREF_ATTRIBUTE patterns restrict schemes to http/https/ftp/mailto plus relative paths.
candidates.description: getValidHref URL-decodes then XML-unescapes the input, then percent-encodes a limited set of characters (", ', >, <, `, space) and, when a '?' exists, replaces ':' in the query portion. It then calls xssFilter.isValidHref on the transformed string. The transformation order (decode/unescape then partial re-encode) is a classic source of bypass; effectiveness depends entirely on the href Attribute patterns in the active AntiSamy policy (DEFAULT_HREF_ATTRIBUTE lines 72-80, or the 'a'/href attribute loaded from config.xml). The ':'-encoding is applied only from the first '?' onward, not to the scheme portion.
missing_evidence: The active config.xml href attribute pattern was not fully compared against DEFAULT_HREF_ATTRIBUTE for discrepancies.
No runtime test of getValidHref with exotic encodings (double-encoding, mixed case schemes, control characters).
preconditions: A caller uses getValidHref output as an href/src attribute.
Attacker input survives the decode/unescape/re-encode pipeline and still matches an allowed href pattern while being dangerous in a browser.
candidates.title: getValidHref re-decodes and re-unescapes input prior to AntiSamy href policy check

counter_evidence: The cache cap is a deliberate bound to prevent unbounded growth.
check/filter fall back to defaultHandler, which still applies XSS filtering (not a bypass to unfiltered output).
loadPolicy is a non-API method per the in-file comment (lines 163-166).
candidates.description: XSSFilterImpl.loadPolicy stores a new PolicyHandler only when policies.size() < DEFAULT_POLICY_CACHE_SIZE (128); otherwise the supplied stream/handler is silently dropped and the policy is not registered. hasPolicy then returns false and check/filter fall back to defaultHandler. Silent omission means a caller may believe a restrictive policy is active while filtering uses the default policy instead.
missing_evidence: No caller of loadPolicy in this repository.
No documentation of expected behavior when the cap is exceeded.
preconditions: More than 128 distinct policies are loaded.
A caller relies on hasPolicy/loadPolicy semantics to enforce a specific policy, without checking hasPolicy after loadPolicy.
candidates.title: loadPolicy silently ignores policies beyond fixed cache size
